I will keep my year simple and steady. I am 65, so I will not chase crops that need too much labor or too much market guessing. In Quzhou County, the crop pattern I trust most is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I know how to manage them, I can use machinery for most work, and grain is easier for me to sell and store than vegetables or cash crops. At the start of this season, I will continue managing the winter wheat already in the field, then after harvest I will plant summer maize right away. I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I want more stable emergence and yield, but I will avoid anything too fancy or expensive. For wheat, I will focus on topdressing nitrogen, watering at the key stages, and controlling aphids and disease if they show up. After wheat harvest, I will return to the field quickly, do light tillage, sow maize in time, and keep fertilizer and irrigation moderate because I do not want to overspend. My goal is steady output, manageable work, and lower risk.
